steps.title: Prepare serum‑free media (SFM)
steps.instruction: Mix a 1:1 mixture of Eagle's MEM and Ham's F‑12; supplement with glucose 6 mg/mL, progesterone 20 nM, putrescine 60 µM, transferrin 100 µg/mL, selenium 30 nM, penicillin 0.5 U/mL, and streptomycin 0.5 µg/mL. Sterile‑filter and keep at 4 °C. Neurobasal media may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Prepare positive relief mold
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean the resin mold, measure its internal volume, and dry it before PDMS casting.

substeps.instruction: Release pressurized air onto the mold surface 5–10 times using a thin tube attached to a 1,000 µL pipette tip moved over the surface to blast away residual PDMS.
Measure mold volume by filling the cavity with DI water, then transfer the water to a 50 mL Falcon tube; record the volume for later PDMS calculations.
Fill the mold cavity with isopropanol and place on a shaker at medium speed for 20 min.
Remove isopropanol and dry the mold uncovered in an oven at 70 °C for 10 min or until completely dry.
Cover the mold to prevent particulate contamination.

steps.title: Cast PDMS devices
steps.instruction: Mix Sylgard 184 base and curing agent, degas, pour into the cleaned mold, and cure.

substeps.instruction: Combine PDMS base and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio in a 50 mL Falcon tube, using the previously measured mold volume to determine the total PDMS volume needed.
Place the mixture on a low‑speed rotator for 20 min until homogeneous.
Pour the PDMS mixture into the mold, starting at a corner and allowing it to flow across the surface to fill the cavity completely.
Place the mold with PDMS in a vacuum desiccator at full suction for 4–5 h, checking bubble disappearance every 2 h.
When the PDMS appears clear and bubble‑free, gently release the desiccator without spilling the liquid PDMS.
Transfer the mold with PDMS to an oven set at 70 °C and bake uncovered for 48 h.

steps.title: Clean and cut PDMS chambers
steps.instruction: Remove cured PDMS from the mold, separate individual chambers, punch inlet/outlet holes, and sterilize.

substeps.instruction: Allow the baked PDMS to cool to room temperature; keep the mold covered.
Using a flat‑tapered spatula and a sharp scalpel, cut the edges of the PDMS block and peel it from the positive‑relief mold.
Each casting yields nine chambers; keep them together until punching.
Punch four holes (size No. 6 biopsy puncher) on the edges of each chamber’s microfluidic channels to create media reservoirs.
Cut each chamber out of the block with a scalpel, trimming the corners so the device fits a 25 mm glass coverslip without overhang.
Remove loose PDMS debris from the negatively etched surface with scotch tape.
Wash the chambers in 70 % ethanol for 10 min.
Dry the chambers at 70 °C for 10 min and store them in a sterile Petri dish.

steps.title: Sterilize devices and coverslips
steps.instruction: Sterilize microfluidic devices and glass coverslips one day before cell seeding.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the PDMS chambers in 70 % ethanol for 10 min inside a laminar‑flow hood; allow them to air‑dry completely.
Place sterile 25 mm glass coverslips in 35 mm Petri dishes.

steps.title: Precoat coverslips with poly‑d‑lysine
steps.instruction: Coat glass coverslips with poly‑d‑lysine to promote cell adhesion.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of poly‑d‑lysine solution (0.2 mg/mL) to each coverslip.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a cell‑culture incubator.
On the day of culture, carefully suction off the poly‑d‑lysine solution without scratching the coated surface.

steps.title: Assemble devices on coverslips
steps.instruction: Bond each sterilized PDMS chamber to a pre‑coated coverslip to create a watertight microfluidic system.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the PDMS chambers are completely dry.
Using sterile forceps, place the negatively etched surface of the PDMS chamber onto the coated coverslip.
Gently press each corner to achieve a tight, water‑tight seal.

steps.title: Harvest E15 embryos
steps.instruction: Euthanize a pregnant mouse and collect embryos at embryonic day 15 under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Expose the pregnant mouse to CO₂ until euthanasia is confirmed.
Soak the mouse in 70 % ethanol for 5 min for surface sterilization.
Make a midline abdominal incision with thick scissors, then cut the muscle layer to expose the uterine horns.
Remove embryos with small scissors, place each embryo in a 20 cm sterile Petri dish containing PBS, and keep the dish on ice.

steps.title: Dissect basal forebrain tissue
steps.instruction: Isolate the medial septum and diagonal band from each embryo in serum‑free media.

substeps.instruction: Transfer embryos to SFM in a laminar‑flow hood.
Using fine straight‑edged forceps, remove each embryo from its amniotic sac and place the head in a separate PBS dish on ice.
Anchor the ventral side of the head with one forceps while gripping the soft skull roof with another; peel off the skull by pulling in opposite directions to expose the brain.
Turn the head sideways and slide the brain out; cut off the olfactory bulbs and frontal cortical poles with sharp scalpels.
Orient the brain with the ventral side up and the olfactory bulbs (rostral) to the left; make a coronal cut at the rostral edge of the hypothalamus to obtain a thick coronal slab.
Rotate the slab 90° so the rostral cut faces upward.
Make dorsal incisions at the tips of the lateral ventricles on both hemispheres and a ventral incision to free the medial septum together with portions of the diagonal band.
Collect the separated septum and diagonal band into a small 30 mm Petri dish containing SFM.
Repeat the dissection for all embryos, pooling the basal forebrain tissue.
Cut the pooled tissue into small pieces in 500 µL–1 mL of SFM (aim for ~2–3 × 10⁶ cells/mL).
Dissociate the tissue by trituration with a Pasteur pipette 20–30 times until a cloudy cell suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Plate basal forebrain cholinergic neurons
steps.instruction: Seed dissociated cells into the soma compartment of each microfluidic device and establish a media gradient.

substeps.instruction: Count cells with a hemocytometer; pipette 50,000 cells in a brief pressure pulse into one side of the chamber (the soma compartment).
Prepare SFM supplemented with 1 % B‑27 (SFM + 1 % B27).
Five minutes after seeding, add 200 µL of SFM + 1 % B27 to each reservoir of the soma compartment.
Add 100 µL of SFM + 1 % B27 to each reservoir of the opposite (axon) compartment.
Maintain the volume gradient for five days at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to promote axonal growth through the microgrooves.
Every alternate day, add 50 µL of fresh SFM + 1 % B27 to all reservoirs to compensate for evaporation.

steps.title: Retrograde tracer labeling
steps.instruction: Label axon‑projecting neurons with Alexa‑488 cholera toxin B and prepare propidium iodide for death detection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a working solution of CTB at 1 µg/mL in SFM.
At 5 days in vitro (DIV), add the CTB solution to the axon compartment and incubate for 20 min in the incubator.
Wash the axon compartment twice with SFM + 1 % B27 to remove excess tracer, then add 100 µL of SFM + 1 % B27 to maintain the axons.
Incubate the cultures for at least 5 h to allow retrograde transport of CTB to the somata.

Immediately before any experimental treatment, replace the soma‑compartment media with SFM + 1 % B27 containing propidium iodide (PI) at 1 µg/mL; incubate for 10 min (PI does not need to be washed out).
Keep the established media‑volume gradient throughout the subsequent treatment.

steps.title: Live imaging setup and acquisition
steps.instruction: Configure the microscope for live imaging and capture fluorescence at defined time points.

substeps.instruction: Place the culture chamber on a microscope stage equipped with temperature (37 °C) and CO₂ (5 %) control for the entire imaging period.
Select a 10× objective and locate the microgroove region using bright‑field so that both soma and axon compartments are in view.
Configure the 488 nm (CTB) and 555 nm (PI) laser lines at low power (5 %–10 %) to minimize phototoxicity; adjust digital offset and gain as needed.
Set the camera to capture 1,024 × 1,024 pixels at a scan speed of 8; maintain these settings for the whole experiment.
Immediately after adding any treatment, acquire fluorescence images of the soma compartment at 0 h (both 488 nm and 555 nm channels).
Return the plate to the incubator for 24 h, or keep it on the microscope stage for continuous time‑lapse imaging, acquiring images at the desired intervals.
Capture a second set of fluorescence images of the soma compartment at the 24 h time point.
After imaging is complete, fix the cells in situ with 4 % paraformaldehyde while the PDMS device remains attached to the coverslip (optional for downstream immunolabeling).
If further processing is required, carefully remove the PDMS device from the coverslip after fixation.
